research.title: Research
research.description: I study how to decode language from non-invasive brain signals such as EEG. Explore the brain regions involved in hearing and speaking.

brain.credit: Brain surface: Brain for Blender by Anderson Winkler, CC BY-SA 3.0. Regions follow the Desikan-Killiany atlas.

auditory.name: Primary auditory cortex
auditory.note: The primary auditory area is the main cortical site that receives signals from the ear. Here it is shown as the transverse temporal region of the atlas.

wernicke.name: Wernicke's area (approximate)
wernicke.note: Wernicke's area lies in the back part of the left superior temporal gyrus. The coloured atlas regions are larger than the area itself. It is known for language comprehension. A 2026 study in Science also found a subregion that becomes active before speech and codes whole upcoming words.

broca.name: Broca's area
broca.note: Broca's area lies in the back part of the left inferior frontal gyrus. It covers the pars opercularis and the pars triangularis, and it is vital for language.

motor.name: Primary motor cortex
motor.note: The precentral gyrus holds the primary motor cortex, which controls voluntary movement. Speaking is one such movement. My channel-selection study includes the left central EEG channels C5, C3 and C1, which sit over the sensorimotor region.

somatosensory.name: Primary somatosensory cortex
somatosensory.note: The postcentral gyrus receives sensory information from the body, such as touch, temperature and pain.

pathway.auditory: 1. Sound signals arrive at the primary auditory cortex.
pathway.wernicke: 2. The posterior superior temporal gyrus supports the understanding of speech. A 2026 study found that part of it also plans upcoming words.
pathway.broca: 3. The arcuate fasciculus (dark line, schematic) links the posterior temporal lobe with the frontal language area.
pathway.motor: 4. The primary motor cortex drives the voluntary movements of speaking.

research.title: Semantic Speech Reconstruction from Cognitive Signals
research.description: Research on reading what a person is trying to say directly from brain activity. Instead of guessing one word out of a fixed list, the goal is to recover the meaning a person intends to express from non-invasive cognitive signals such as EEG. The motivation is communication support for people who have lost the ability to speak, where reconstructing intent at the semantic level is far more useful than classifying individual syllables.

isp.title: Multi-Tenant ISP Operations Platform
isp.description: Operations and business support system for internet service providers, serving multiple operator tenants from a single deployment. Covers subscriber lifecycle, billing, provisioning, and a real-time telemetry service that ingests PPPoE session data from network equipment and aggregates usage into half-hourly, daily, and monthly analytics. Jobs run on a Redis-backed queue with strict idempotency guarantees; production monitoring is built on AWS CloudWatch with Slack alerting.

pos.title: Restaurant POS & Kitchen Display
pos.description: Point-of-sale platform for restaurants with a web-based admin dashboard, cross-platform kitchen display (KDS), and device-bound authentication. Designed for reliability in low-connectivity environments with offline order capture and deterministic sync on reconnect. Covers menu management, order routing to stations, and end-of-day reconciliation.

chatbot.title: Education Chatbot for Non-Profit
chatbot.description: Multi-channel learning chatbot (Messenger, Viber, Telegram) delivering curricula, quizzes, and certification to users across Myanmar. Built as the primary engagement surface for a youth-empowerment non-profit, paired with an internal admin dashboard for content authoring, user support, and impact reporting.
